chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Muhammad! Had the beggar known what is in the begging, no one would beg from anyone; and had the giver known what is in the giving, no one would have repelled anyone'.

key_terms.السَّائِلُ: The beggar or one who asks
key_terms.الْمَسْأَلَةُ: The act of asking or the question itself

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of begging and giving charity according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) highlights the spiritual gravity of the transaction between beggar and giver, suggesting that the 'hidden consequence' (often interpreted as the erosion of dignity or the accumulation of spiritual debt) is sufficient to deter both parties if fully realized. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on preserving self-respect (*ghina*) and the sincerity of charity, warning that the act of asking or giving is not merely material but a profound spiritual exchange. The Imam’s address to 'Muhammad' (likely referring to the companion or the general believer) serves to personalize this universal truth, urging mindfulness in every act of supplication and generosity.
